steps: Create two tracks reusing one registered WAV and review exact source/relations. Chinese, English and Japanese at 390px preserve the pending values, identities and approved source. Cancel writes no author files.

One Save creates exactly the reviewed audio source, its registration and the scene audio relation. Two tracks bind one deduplicated resource; source scene, WAV and other author bytes remain unchanged.
Open audio source enters the existing ordinary editor. Independent field review/application changes only the unsaved draft; ordinary Save updates exactly that audio JSON.
Reopening scene audio settings resolves the existing document and offers source editing without allocating or duplicating another audio manifest.
The same scene plans, builds and runs through real Godot. The host validates two audio commands (music play and effect play at 0.125s) and independent audio/actor completion.

Chrome downloads the generated engine project ZIP. Independent verification confirms one deduplicated WAV resource, extraction preserves its exact bytes and settings, and fresh Godot import/run at another path produces identical audio events.

limitations: Actual Chrome using the local HTTP editor and trusted native Godot. No installed Tauri window, native file picker, Android or other desktop OS claim.
The scene-audio example is copied and its audio document/opt-in removed. Two tracks are created using an already registered WAV; resource import and upstream scene creation are outside this test.
Godot runs bounded headless logic with two audio commands. This browser workflow makes no speaker or audible-output claim; native PCM mixer capture is verified separately.
Generated project ZIP is downloaded by Chrome, independently verified, extracted and run at a new path. It is source-engineering delivery, not a standalone game executable.
